title: Uniform affine étale cohomology bound for finite coefficient module sheaves
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite or algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $A$ a finite commutative ring with $\ell^aA=0$ for some integer $a\geq1$. Let $X$ be a finite-type $k$-scheme and $w:W\to X$ an affine étale object of its small étale site [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Work in a common larger universe in which the sites are small [def-weil-size-convention]. Put $d_X=\dim X$ if $X\ne\varnothing$ and $d_X=0$ if $X=\varnothing$, and put $e_X=2d_X+1$, with topological Krull dimension as in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Use constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and ordinary left module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For every sheaf $G$ of $A_X$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ and every integer $q>e_X$, one has
$$H^q_A(W_{\mathrm{ét}},w_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}G)=0.$$
Here $w_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}$ is inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], and $H^q_A$ is right-derived global sections in the module-sheaf category: choose an injective resolution of $w_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}G$ on $W_{\mathrm{ét}}$, evaluate it at $W$, and take degree-$q$ cohomology [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. There is no constructibility, finite-generation, or coefficient-flatness assumption on $G$.

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation: the torsion-to-étale-module sheaf bound; Stacks Tag 099W (proetale-lemma-compare-cohomology) and Tag 03FD (sites-cohomology-lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), applied to the blueprint uniform torsion bound.

proof.text: Write $F$ for the underlying abelian sheaf of $G$. Put $N=\ell^a>0$. For any étale object $V\to X$ and $s\in F(V)$, the constant scalar $N1_A$ has zero image in $A_X(V)$, since $NA=0$. Thus $Ns=(N1_A)s=0$ by the module axioms. In particular every section is killed by the same positive integer, so $F$ is a torsion abelian sheaf. This argument imposes no finiteness condition on $F(V)$.

source.place: Opening paragraph: every A-module sheaf is torsion

proof.text: The étale map $w:W\to X$ is weakly étale by Mathlib’s instance from étale morphisms, hence defines an object of $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ in the chosen universes. Give $W$ the constant presentation indexed by the category with one object and only its identity: its unique stage is the affine scheme $W$, its stage map to $X$ is $w$, and its transition is $\mathrm{id}_W$, which is affine. This category is small, nonempty and cofiltered. The identity cone has the inverse-limit universal property, since a cone is just one map to $W$. It therefore is a presentation of the type specified in [sk-def-pe-morphisms].

source.place: Fixed-degree truncation, constant presentation of W

proof.text: Apply part (1) of [det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds] to the torsion abelian sheaf $F$ on $X$, and to the one-stage presentation just constructed. In the theorem take $Y=X$ and $g=\mathrm{id}_X$, a finite-type morphism: on each affine chart its ring map is the identity, generated by the empty set. The field and finite-type hypotheses on $X$ are the given ones. Its empty-scheme convention is exactly our $d_X$, so its bound is exactly $e_X=2d_X+1$. We obtain $H^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},w_{\mathrm{proét}}^{-1}\nu_X^*F)=0$ for every integer $q>e_X$.

source.place: Part (1), specialized to the constant presentation

proof.text:
Put $F_W=w_{\mathrm{ét}}^{-1}F$. The source library’s canonical comparisonUpperStarCompUpperStarIso, obtained by composition of the inverse-image adjunctions, identifies $
u_W^*F_W$ with $w_{\mathrm{proét}}^{-1}
u_X^*F$, the coefficient sheaf in the previous step. Since $e_X\geq1$, the integer $q>e_X$ is nonnegative. Apply [lem-cbc-abelian-etale-proetale-cohomology-comparison] on the scheme $W$ in degree $q$ to obtain $$H^q(W_{\mathrm{ét}},F_W)\cong H^q(W_{\mathrm{proét}},
u_W^*F_W)=0.$$ Both comparisons concern abelian sheaves, and neither requires constructibility.

The constant-ring module realization leaves the abelian sheaf unchanged. The canonical upperStarForget₂Comparison, which is an isomorphism, identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of the displayed module inverse image with the abelian inverse image. Transfer abelian cohomology vanishing along this isomorphism.

The constant-ring module equivalence supplies enough injectives from the Grothendieck category of module-valued sheaves. Its inverse restriction functor takes injectives to injectives. For finite A, the already-proved finite-coefficient acyclicity theorem makes their underlying abelian sheaves acyclic for terminal-object evaluation. Forgetting ring-module structure is exact. Apply the exact-composite derived-functor comparison to identify abelian derived evaluation with the cohomology of the chosen module resolution after scalar forgetting. Exact scalar forgetting commutes with homology. Its faithfulness reflects equality of the identity and zero, hence reflects the zero object.

proof_origin.place: The original constant-presentation geometric route, followed by the proved finite-ring acyclicity and exact-composite comparison at the actual site universes.

Checked empty schemes, zero coefficients, nonconstructible sheaves, source clauses and the dependency closure. No new nodes.

tool_uses.why: Its clause (1) verifies that the étale test object is an object of the pro-étale site; this is a generic geometric input, not a replacement of the unit route.
The explicit uniform torsion bound is the input named by the blueprint fixed-degree truncation paragraph; we use its part (1) on the constant presentation.
The comparison square identifies the coefficient on W; no node in the present unit states this generic compatibility.
Stacks 099W transfers the abelian vanishing from the constant pro-étale presentation back to the étale site, as the item source specifies.
The general constant-coefficient inverse-image theorem identifies the underlying abelian sheaf of the module pullback, required to keep coefficient categories exact.
This standard small-ringed-site tool verifies the enough-injectives hypothesis in the module/abelian cohomology comparison.
This is the Stacks 03FD comparison for ordinary ring-sheaf modules, which supplies the module bound from abelian vanishing; the unit has no different coefficient comparison.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q30-5bd05ede4 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all six steps and every cited statement. Step 1: N=ℓ^a kills every section, so F is torsion in the sense of def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves. Step 2: étale implies weakly étale (det-pe-morphisms-etale-comparison (1)), and the one-object presentation of W meets every condition of sk-def-pe-morphisms; the blueprint unit proof itself says 'W (with the constant presentation)'. Step 3: det-pe-unbounded-classical-bounds (1) with Y=X and g=id; e_X matches, including the empty convention. Step 4: lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback plus lem-cbc (Stacks 099W, proetale.tex l.3986, part (1); any abelian sheaf, i≥0, and q>e_X≥1). Step 5: lem-pe-constant-left-module-inverse-image (00YV) gives (w^{-1}G)_ab=F_W, consistent with def-weil-pbc-inverse-image acting on module sheaves. Step 6: enough injectives and the ringed-site evaluation comparison (Stacks 03FD, sites-cohomology.tex l.1862, 'any object U'), which is exactly the item's H^q_A. The statement is exactly what parent lem-sfb-unbounded-site-comparison step 5 uses, and it is not weakened. Edge cases tested: X empty, W empty, A=0, a point over F_q or k̄, and non-constructible or non-flat G. No cycle: no cited node's closure reaches the item. I searched for duplicates (thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd, lem-sfb-classical-module-affine-evaluation-bound, the bounds node, sk-def-cd) and found none stating the étale module bound. There are no new nodes and no SGA citations. TeX, proof_deps and the 10 recorded searches are in order.
